subject.title: Config: scaffold compaction loop guard settings

question: Should OpenClaw accept `agents.defaults.compaction.guard` as a public config contract before runtime compaction-guard behavior lands?
rationale: The branch is narrow, but the root policy treats new config/default surfaces as compatibility-sensitive and current main has no matching runtime semantics for the proposed guard keys.

options.title: Hold for maintainer-owned guard contract
options.body: Keep this PR open only as context while maintainers decide the final compaction guard config and request a refreshed, proof-backed branch if the shape is accepted.

options.title: Close in favor of the canonical issue
options.body: Close this PR if maintainers want the broader issue to own the design and later implementation instead of preserving this stale scaffold branch.

options.title: Sponsor and refresh this branch
options.body: A maintainer can adopt the branch, resolve conflicts, add upgrade proof, and land it if this exact config surface is the intended public contract.

recommendation.title: Hold for maintainer-owned guard contract
recommendation.body: Keep this PR open only as context while maintainers decide the final compaction guard config and request a refreshed, proof-backed branch if the shape is accepted.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main history connects this owner to config/default surfaces and broad agent-runtime refactors, making them the best available routing candidate for the API-contract decision.
